lines.text: Marvel Mystery Oil costs half as much as Seafoam so can it really clean an engine just as well?
Seafoam already cleaned carbon off a piston in his last test and that black crust steals compression from an engine.
beats: ai:thick black carbon deposits crusted on top of an engine piston macro

lines.text: So he tests this mower first and it already makes 105 psi cold which is very good compression for a small engine.
Viewers claimed the oil drains into the crankcase but that tube runs uphill so he tapes it shut anyway.
beats: ai:a black rubber breather hose running uphill from a carburetor on a small mower engine close up

lines.text: Then he hangs a bag like a hospital drip so 8 ounces of Marvel feeds slowly into the carburetor.
beats: ai:a clear hospital IV drip bag hanging from a metal stand with a thin tube

lines.text: And the mower blows thick white smoke because the oil is burning off inside the hot cylinder.
beats: ai:oil mist burning inside a glowing hot engine cylinder close up

lines.text: Then he fills the cylinder and lets it soak for 20 minutes and after that it runs great without smoke.
But hot compression doesn't budge because the gauge reads 106 before and 106 after which is exactly zero gain.
Seafoam gained more in his last test but that engine started much weaker so it had way more room to improve.
beats: ai:a small engine compression gauge needle slowly climbing higher close up

lines.text: So is Seafoam worth the extra money?
